title: Timeline prints an invisible placeholder for an unreadable app message whose text is only the object-replacement character
description:
Found 2026-11-14 during imessage-exporter-djf.2; fixed in 8bf1f5e4 (awaiting review). When upstream's balloon dispatcher returns an error, the timeline's App arm prints its pre-djf.2 output (djf.2's decision): the message text in italics, or `*[App message]*` when the text is empty after trimming. An app message's text is often only U+FFFC (the object-replacement character), which is not whitespace, so the fallback printed `*￼*`: an italic invisible character, with no error reported anywhere (TXT prints `Unable to format app message: <error>` instead).

## Fix (landed)
- app_message_fallback (imessage-exporter/src/exporters/timeline.rs) treats text made only of U+FFFC and whitespace as empty, so it prints `*[App message]*`. Text with real characters next to U+FFFC is unchanged.

## Measured before the fix

- Synthetic seeded fixture (/tmp/claude-501/imx-test/fixture-apps/chat.db, row fx-broken-app: an app balloon with no payload and a U+FFFC body): the timeline printed `*￼*`; TXT prints `Unable to format app message: Failed to parse property list: Unable to acquire payload data!`.

title: Lines of only = or - under a message line render as headings in the timeline export
description:
Found 2026-11-14 during imessage-exporter-djf.9. djf.9 escapes message and balloon lines that read as ATX headings (`# x`), but not setext headings: in Markdown, a line made only of `=` or `-` (0-3 spaces of indentation) directly under a line of text turns that text line into an H1 (`=`) or H2 (`-`). A message such as "Total\n-----" therefore renders as a heading in the timeline. Tools that split the file on `^#` lines are not affected; Markdown renderers and outline views are.

## Measured on the May real-db copy (counts only, 2026-11-14, djf.9 binary 50e65059)
- 128 lines made only of `=` or `-` sit directly under a non-blank line (`rg -c -U` over the export; an upper bound, since rg's multiline count may count both lines of a match).

## Fix shape (needs a small decision)
- Option a: in escape_heading_lines (imessage-exporter/src/exporters/timeline.rs), also put a backslash before the first `=` or `-` of such an underline line when the previous line is text. Renders as the literal characters.
- Option b: leave it; setext headings do not break day or thread counting.
- Fork-owned code only. Note `---` after a blank line is a thematic break (horizontal rule), not a heading; option a need not touch it.

title: Fix the eleven problems the full code review found in the timeline export, -w and the database hint
description:
Findings from the independent full review of all fork-owned code (2026-11-14, branch worktree-upstream-5-sync at e633c70c, base upstream 47b75148). Every finding was confirmed by running the release binary on synthetic fixtures (under /tmp/claude-501/imx-test/fixture-review/: chat.db, chat-inline.db, chat-dangling.db, chat-lookup.db, seed.sql) or by reading, as marked. All fixes go in fork-owned code only; `git diff --stat 47b75148 HEAD -- imessage-database` stays empty and txt/, html/, shared/, formatter.rs stay untouched. Conductor decisions (taken under Justin's overnight instruction to use the recommended option) are stated per finding.

## Group A — timeline output (imessage-exporter/src/exporters/timeline.rs, timeline_balloons.rs)

F1 (serious, confirmed). One message can turn the rest of timeline.md into a code block. escape_heading_lines escapes only ATX headings. A line that opens a fence (0-3 spaces, then ``` or ~~~) or an HTML block of CommonMark types 1-5 (`<!--`, `<pre`, `<script`, `<style`, `<textarea`, `<?`, `<!` + letter, `<![CDATA[`) passes through; with no closing fence, every later message, day heading and thread heading renders inside it (pandoc CommonMark: 1 h1 instead of 3). Fix: extend the same escape pass (rename it to fit, e.g. escape_block_starts) to put a backslash before a fence opener and before `<` on lines that open HTML block types 1-5. Also fold in djf.11: escape a setext underline (a line of only `=` or only `-`, 0-3 spaces indent, directly under a non-blank text line) so it cannot turn the previous line into a heading — simplest correct shape: backslash before the first `=`/`-` of such a line inside message/balloon text. Handwriting's raw_line fence stays raw. Same call sites as today.

F2 (serious, confirmed). Every reply appears twice, and the nested copy sits under the parent's day showing only a time of day, so a reply sent on Feb 7 reads as sent on Feb 6. Decision: keep both copies, as upstream TXT does, and make each one unambiguous. (a) In the nested (blockquoted) copy, when the reply's local date differs from the parent's date, the header shows the full date and time (e.g. `**Fri, Feb 7, 2025 1:25:24 PM — Me**`). (b) The standalone copy, under its own day, gets one italic line right after its header: `*(reply to a message from <full date and time of the parent>)*`. If the parent cannot be found, use `*(reply to an earlier message)*`.

F3 (confirmed). An attachment is dropped when one text bubble holds several inline stickers or genmoji, and later bubbles can be paired with the wrong attachment: the timeline pairs attachments by position and names at most one per bubble. Fix: use upstream's GUID pairing — iterate `resolve_run(ranges, &mut AttachmentResolver::new(&attachments))` (shared/part.rs) and print one label per attachment range, keeping the sticker/attachment labels from djf.8. Test with upstream's typedstream fixture FormattedInlineStickers.

F7 (confirmed, rare). A message whose date cannot be converted is dropped silently (`Err(_) => return Ok(())` at the date step). Fix: count it in skipped_messages and print a stderr line in the same shape as djf.7's `Skipping message (rowid=…, guid=…): <error>`.

F8 (confirmed by reading). A failed export truncates the previous timeline.md before iteration, leaving a 0-byte file. Fix: write to a temporary file in the same directory and rename it over timeline.md only on success (or open the file only at flush time). A failed run must leave an existing timeline.md byte-identical.

F10 (confirmed by reading). Thread headings reuse Config::filename, which truncates to 235 minus the export path length and replaces characters not allowed in file names, so a long -o path or a group name with `/` or `:` changes the heading. Fix: build the heading from the chat's display name, else the participant names (the same names Config::filename would use, untruncated and unsanitized), else the chat identifier; keep the per-chat cache from djf.5 and its once-per-chat warning behavior. The heading must not depend on the -o path.

## Group B — -w selection, options and the database hint

F4 (confirmed). A -w group whose names all resolve but matches no chat exactly is dropped silently (e.g. `-w alice -w alice,carol` with Carol only in a group that also has Bob exports the Alice DM, exit 0, no warning). Decision: print a stderr warning naming the group (`Warning: --conversation-with group `alice,carol` matched no conversation`), keep exporting the groups that matched; the existing all-groups-empty error stays.

F5 (confirmed on synthetic data). -w selects chat rows, not merged conversations: upstream merges chat rows through chat_lookup (ChatToHandle::dedupe, Config.real_chatrooms), and a sibling row with a different participant set or no participant rows is never selected, so part of a conversation goes missing under the same heading. Fix: after exact matching, also select every chat row whose real_chatrooms id equals a matched row's real_chatrooms id.

F6 (confirmed, damaged DB only). -w drops handles with no handle row (`filter_map(|h| self.real_participants.get(h))`), so a chat {Alice, 77} matches `-w alice` as a DM. Fix: treat an unknown handle as its own distinct participant so the set no longer equals {Alice}.

F9 (confirmed by reading). - Fields one per line: TXT's connecting words that only name the balloon are dropped, because the italic label names it: `<app> message:` (Fitness, Collaboration, generic), ` transaction:` (Apple Pay), `Photo album:` (Slideshow), the `:` joining Find My's name and status. - Find My shows `*Find My*` then `Find My` (app_name) then the status: strict field parity repeats the name. Same can happen for Fitness. Cosmetic.
- Fields are written one per line with no hard line breaks. Strict CommonMark renderers join consecutive lines into one paragraph; editors that render single newlines as breaks (Obsidian's default) show them on separate lines. Lists (poll, business) render as lists either way.
- Handwriting always renders as ASCII art inside a ``` fence. TXT writes a file when attachment copying is on; the timeline never copies attachments, so it uses TXT's copy-disabled output. - Autolinks only for absolute URIs (CommonMark scheme rule); a bare `example.com` from msg.text stays plain, since `<example.com>` would show literally or parse as an HTML tag.
- Generic app label: app_name, else bundle ID, else `App`. TXT uses app_name even when it is an empty string and then prints no label.
- The fallback is silent: no stderr line per failed balloon (TXT prints the error into the export). Rule 7 check: the fallback output is the old visible text or placeholder, never a neutral value.
- rewrite_fitness_receiver: TXT uses it on text bubbles (body_text_with_translation), not in any balloon method, so it is applied in the timeline's Run arm. This touches text output only when a line starts with the Fitness receiver placeholder.
- TXT's view models (txt/view_model.rs) are pub(super), so the timeline cannot reuse them; it reuses upstream's OptionalText and resolve_check_in_footer and builds lines directly. No upstream visibility widened.

description:
Make the "can't open the Messages database" error tell the user exactly what to do on macOS. Justin hit this on 2026-05-10: "I don't think the issue is full disk access -- I can access the chat.db file from the terminal." His terminal had Full Disk Access; the exporter still could not open chat.db. Upstream's message (imessage-database/src/error/table.rs, const FULL_DISK_ACCESS) only says to enable Full Disk Access for the terminal emulator, which he had already done.

## Status (2026-11-14): built and verified on worktree-upstream-5-sync in commits f2cf7624 and bceae138 (copy folder mode 700); not pushed, not merged
- New fork-owned file imessage-exporter/src/db_access_hint.rs:
  - db_access_hint(Option<PathBuf>) -> String: the pure hint builder. An empty path counts as None.
  - is_db_access_error(&RuntimeError): true only for DatabaseError(CannotConnect(Permissions(_) | Inaccessible(..))), the two variants upstream ends with its Full Disk Access line.
  - eprint_db_access_hint(&RuntimeError): holds the cfg!(target_os = "macos") gate, calls std::env::current_exe(), prints the hint to stderr.
- imessage-exporter/src/main.rs: one `mod db_access_hint;` line, and one eprint_db_access_hint(&why) call after each of the three error prints ("Invalid configuration" for Config::new, and the two "Unable to export" prints for resolve_filtered_handles and start).
- imessage-database is unchanged: git diff 47b75148 -- imessage-database is empty.

## The hint as printed (after upstream's two lines)
    If your terminal already has Full Disk Access and this still fails, add this program itself in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access:
        <absolute path from current_exe>
    Or copy the database to a folder you can read and point at the copy:
        mkdir -p -m 700 /tmp/imx && cp ~/Library/Messages/chat.db* /tmp/imx/
        imessage-exporter -p /tmp/imx/chat.db <your other options>
The copy folder is created mode 700 so other local accounts cannot read the copied message history (conductor decision, 2026-11-14). mkdir sets the mode only when it creates the folder; an existing /tmp/imx keeps its mode.
When current_exe fails or returns an empty path, the first sentence reads "... add this program itself (the imessage-exporter binary you ran) in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access." and no path line is printed. The hint states no cause.

## Out of scope
- Detecting Full Disk Access status programmatically (TCC queries).
- Changing upstream's message text, other error kinds, or Linux/Windows behavior.

## No knob
Message text with no sane "off" state (feature-knobs rule: no switch needed).

- A test-only counter (`#[cfg(test)] computed`) counts cache misses for the unit test.
- Config::filename (upstream-owned) is unchanged.

title: Keep the timeline export going when one message cannot be read, the way the txt and html exports do
description:
Fixed in e836ce82 (awaiting review). In imessage-exporter/src/exporters/timeline.rs, format_timeline_message uses ? on Attachment::from_message and msg.get_replies, and iter_messages passed that error up, so one unreadable message ended the whole timeline export (exit 1, empty timeline.md). Upstream's shared driver (exporters/shared/driver.rs), used by txt and html, reports such a message and continues. Found by the 2026-11-14 upstream-sync review; the May database copy hits no such error, so this is a robustness fix, not an observed failure.

## Fix (landed)
- iter_messages matches on format_timeline_message. On an error it prints `Skipping message (rowid=<rowid>, guid=<guid>): <error>` on stderr, counts it in the new `skipped_messages` field, leaves the message out and goes on. After the progress bar finishes it prints `<N> messages skipped due to formatting errors.` when N > 0. Both lines are worded exactly as upstream's driver words them.
- Same granularity as upstream: the whole top-level message is skipped, and a reply that cannot be read still skips its parent (TXT's build_replies also propagates with ?).
- Unchanged: a row that cannot be read from the message query itself (`let msg = message?`) still ends the export, as in upstream's driver.

title: Lines that start with # in a message or balloon look like day or thread headings in the timeline export
description:
Found 2026-11-14 during imessage-exporter-djf.2; fixed in 50e65059 (awaiting review). The timeline wrote message text and app balloon fields as is, so a line of text that starts with `# ` or `## ` read as a day heading (H1) or a thread heading (H2): Markdown rendered it as a heading, and any reader or tool that splits the file on headings miscounted days and threads.

## Fix (landed, decision option a, narrowed)
- `escape_heading_lines` (imessage-exporter/src/exporters/timeline.rs): a line that CommonMark reads as an ATX heading (0-3 spaces, then 1-6 `#`, then a space, a tab or the end of the line) gets a backslash before its first `#`; Markdown renders it as a plain `#`. Lines end at `\n` or `\r`. Hashtags (`#blessed`), 7+ `#` and lines indented 4+ spaces are left alone. Escaping is idempotent.
- Applied, in fork-owned code only, to: message body text (Run parts and the no-components fallback), the subject, the app fallback text (app_message_fallback), and every balloon line built through `Balloon::line`/`field`/`url` (timeline_balloons.rs). Replies are formatted (and so escaped) before they are blockquoted, so a reply line becomes `> \# …`.
- Not escaped: the handwriting ASCII art inside its ``` fence (new `Balloon::raw_line`; a backslash would show literally in code), the headings the timeline writes itself, announcement lines and tapback lines (they start with `*` or `- `).

## Known gaps left alone (outside the narrowed decision)
- Heading markers after a list marker or a typed blockquote marker (`- # x`, `> # x`): Markdown renders a heading inside the list item or quote. Includes poll option and business item text. They are not day or thread headings for a tool that splits on `^#`.
- Setext headings: a line of only `=` or `-` under a text line renders as an H1/H2 in Markdown. Filed as imessage-exporter-djf.11.

## Decision record
Decision (conductor, 2026-11-14, under Justin's overnight instruction to take the recommended option): option a, narrowed, as above. Option b (document only) was rejected because tools and readers that split the file on headings would still miscount days and threads.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Unit tests: '# hi' -> '\# hi'; '## hi' -> '\## hi'; '   # hi' (3 spaces) escaped; '#blessed' unchanged; '####### x' (7 #) unchanged; a heading-shaped line inside a reply's blockquote is escaped. 2. Negative control shown. 3. On the May real-db copy (counts only): lines starting '# ' equal the well-formed day-heading count (3898 on 2026-11-14), and message-header, day and thread-heading counts are otherwise unchanged. 4. Full gate green.
notes:
## Status (2026-11-14)
Built and committed (50e65059, branch worktree-upstream-5-sync). Not pushed or merged. Awaiting conductor review.

## Verification, per acceptance criterion
- AC1 (6 new tests):
  - escape_heading_lines_escapes_only_atx_headings: '# hi' -> '\# hi'; '## hi' -> '\## hi'; '   # hi' -> '   \# hi'; '###### six' escaped; '#' alone and '#<tab>' escaped; '#blessed', '####### x', '    # four spaces', 'a # in the middle', '- # in a list item' and '' unchanged; multi-line text with `\n`, `\r\n` and `\r` escapes only the heading lines.
  - escape_heading_lines_is_idempotent_and_borrows_when_unchanged.
  - heading_shaped_message_lines_are_escaped (end to end through format_timeline_message, including a two-line subject).
  - heading_shaped_reply_line_is_escaped_inside_the_blockquote: seeded parent row 9020 and reply row 9021 (`# reply heading`, thread_originator_guid set) in the test's scratch database; the parent renders `> \# reply heading`.
  - heading_shaped_line_in_app_fallback_text_is_escaped: `*first\n\# second*`.
  - heading_shaped_field_lines_are_escaped (timeline_balloons.rs): generic app title and a second caption line, music lyrics and track name, and a link whose text is not a URL.
- AC2 negative control: escape_heading_lines made a no-op -> 5 tests fail, each on its escape assertion (for example the reply test: left `> # reply heading`, right `> \# reply heading`); the idempotence test passes (expected: a no-op is idempotent). Restored -> all pass.
- AC3, May real-db copy, counts only, djf.8 binary vs this commit: exit 0 both, 1 file both.
  - Lines starting `# `: 3917 -> 3898, equal to the well-formed day headings (3898 both).
  - Lines starting `## `: 38308 -> 38282. 26 of the 38308 were message or balloon text, not 1 as inferred on 2026-11-14 (and 25 before djf.2). The real thread heading count is 38282 before and after: the code that writes headings is untouched, and 38308 - 26 escaped `\## ` lines = 38282.
  - Escaped lines: 83 (19 `\# `, 26 `\## `, 38 deeper or indented). ATX-heading-shaped lines 42263 -> 42180 = 3898 + 38282: after the fix the only heading lines are the day and thread headings.
  - Message headers 218239, reply headers 5846, announcement lines 4696, attachment + sticker placeholders 33333: unchanged. Size +83 bytes, one backslash per escaped line.
  - Synthetic fixture /tmp/claude-501/imx-test/fixture-apps/chat.db: output identical to the djf.8 commit (it has no heading-shaped text).
- AC4: cargo build OK; cargo test --workspace passes (counts in the dispatch report); nightly clippy -D warnings clean; nightly fmt --check clean. bun run signal and the release build are run at the end of the dispatch.

## Judgment calls (review these)
- The subject is escaped too (the decision names body and balloon lines; a subject's later lines are message text the same way).
- `\r` counts as a line ending, as in CommonMark; Messages text can contain a lone `\r`.
- Every `Balloon::line` is escaped, not only `field`: lyrics, Apple Pay and Fitness amounts, poll and business lines. Poll and business lines start with `- `, so their first line never changes; only a later line of a multi-line value can.
- The 2026-11-14 counts for `## ` lines (and the 3p0.1.2 regression check's thread header counts) included about 25 lines of message text; the real thread heading count on the May copy is 38282.
